rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Pheretima's reproductive system is complete in both sexes in one body. The male side: testes in testis sacs at segments 10–11, sperm maturing in seminal vesicles at 9 and 12, conducted by vasa deferentia with prostatic secretions to the male pores at segment 18. The female side: ovaries at segment 13, oviducts to the female pore at 14, and four pairs of spermathecae at 6–9 to store the partner's sperm.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Testes 10 and 11. Vesicles 11 and 12. Ovaries 13. Female pore 14. Male pores 18.
Spermathecae in 6, 7, 8 and 9.
Copulation, then cocoon, then fertilisation, then direct development.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Hermaphrodite does not mean self-fertilising. Pheretima exchanges sperm with another worm.  ·  Fertilisation is not in the oviduct. It is in the cocoon, after both eggs and stored sperm have been shed into it.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Do not invent a larval stage. Direct development is a standard point against the marine annelid larva.  ·  Prostate, accessory gland and spermatheca are three different structures. A labelled diagram that swaps them loses the segment numbers.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Pheretima cocoon*** — clitellar secretion; direct development of 1–20 young.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Nephridia and the nerve cord are the previous note. Digestion is the one before that.  ·  Numbers are for Pheretima posthuma, not for every oligochaete.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Draw a segment map from 6 to 18 marking only reproductive openings and organs.  ·  Write five sentences in time order from copulation to hatching.

rows.label: Board question

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Hermaphrodite with cross-fertilisation:** complete male and female systems in one body, but obligate exchange of sperm — reproductive assurance without losing genetic variation.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Male: testes in sacs (10, 11) → seminal vesicles (9, 12) → vasa deferentia + prostate glands → male pores (18).  ·  Female: ovaries (13) → oviducts → female pore (14); four pairs of spermathecae (6–9) store partner's sperm.  ·  Copulation: ventral apposition, heads opposite; sperm exchanged into spermathecae. Cocoon: clitellar mucus band slides forward, receives ova (14) and sperm; fertilisation in cocoon; direct development; 1–20 young.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Earthworm cocoons can remain dormant through dry seasons and hatch when moisture returns.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Fertilisation in Pheretima occurs → B  ·  Spermathecae store → C

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Spermathecae store the partner's sperm. They are not the ovaries, and they are not the seminal vesicles.  ·  The clitellum secretes the cocoon. It is not itself the cocoon, and it is not shed as a permanent organ.  ·  Segment numbers: male pores 18, female pore 14, spermathecae 6–9, clitellum 14–16.
